hypothesis: An oceanic slab currently underlies the present fold-thrust belt offshore Sabah.

dimensional_entropy_score.interpretation: High entropy across 6/7 dimensions indicates systematic mismatch between predicted slab signatures and observed geology.

SOURCE.detail: No oceanic-crustal source material detected in fold-thrust belt. Observed Vp 3.2-5.5 km/s vs predicted slab Vp 6.8-8.1 km/s. The mass source is continental margin sediments (Baram-Line provenance), NOT oceanic crust.

TRANSFER.detail: No subduction transfer mechanism evidenced. Fold-thrust belt vergence is NE (toward coast), inconsistent with NW-dipping slab. No Wadati-Benioff zone. No trench-forearc system. Deformation transferred via collision/accretion, not subduction.

SINK.detail: No slab sink detected. Expected: deep seismicity, negative tomographic anomaly, slab-dehydration signatures. Observed: shallow seismicity (<50 km), normal geothermal gradient, no slab window or breakoff signal.

BURIAL.detail: Basin fill thickness (5-10 km) is consistent with flexural loading from collision OR slab-induced subsidence. Cannot distinguish between these mechanisms from fill volume alone. The 43% acoustic impedance deficit is diagnostic but non-unique.

EXHUMATION.detail: Crocker Range exhumation is consistent with collision-related uplift (Late Miocene-Pliocene). No slab-dehydration-driven metamorphism. No high-P/low-T metamorphic signature expected from subduction channel. Exhumation pattern fits accretionary prism, not subduction complex.

alternative_model.name: Collision-accretion tectonics (Crocker Formation accretionary prism)

alternative_model.explanation: The fold-thrust belt is the surface expression of the accretionary prism formed by the collision of the Dangerous Grounds (continental) with the Crocker accretionary wedge. No oceanic slab is required. Flexural loading from the accretionary wedge drives basin subsidence. Shallow seismicity reflects crustal deformation, not subduction.

conclusion.direct_answer: No. The oceanic slab does NOT exist beneath the present fold-thrust belt offshore Sabah. All six contrast dimensions (mass, energy, time, space, absence, information) contradict the hypothesis. The 7th dimension (intelligence) shows the collision-accretion model explains 100% of observations vs 0% for the active-slab model.

required_revisions: Reinterpret vergence polarity — the fold-thrust belt would need to verge AWAY from the slab (currently verges NE toward coast)
Postulate a Wadati-Benioff zone at 100-300 km depth beneath Sabah — no seismic evidence exists
Identify a volcanic arc of Neogene age — none exists in Sabah
Explain the 43% acoustic impedance deficit — requires >60% serpentinization of the slab
Reinterpret all shallow seismicity (<50 km) as slab-interface coupling — currently attributed to crustal deformation
what_changes_if_slab_exists.impact: Would fundamentally rewrite Southeast Asian tectonic history, requiring a complete reinterpretation of the Sabah fold-thrust belt from collision-related to subduction-related.

what_changes_if_slab_does_not_exist.confirmation: Current collision-accretion model is upheld. The fold-thrust belt is an accretionary prism driven by continental collision (Dangerous Grounds vs Borneo). Basin subsidence is flexural. Deformation is crustal. No subduction component needed.
what_changes_if_slab_does_not_exist.remaining_question: Was the Proto-South China Sea slab consumed by the Miocene? A relict (cold, detached) slab at >200 km depth is not ruled out by this analysis — only an active, present-day slab is contradicted.
